target_customer: Media outlets, universities, foundations, brands and researchers that pay for surveys and analytics on US college students
problem: It is hard and slow to measure college student opinion at scale; the company built a large student panel with an app for real time polling.
business_model: B2B survey and analytics services sold on a proprietary student panel, with data reports and partnerships

founders.name: Terren Klein
education: Dartmouth College, class of 2017 (Dartmouth news, June 2017)
founders.background_notes: Started the product at Dartmouth's DALI Lab in 2016 per NHBR; Stamps scholar per Dartmouth. NHBR spells the first name Terrin.

founders.name: Robin Jayaswal
education: Dartmouth College, class of 2018 (Dartmouth news, June 2017)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Dartmouth and NHBR; search snippets from a press release give him the CTO title, not opened directly.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile and web survey app plus panel management and weighting is standard engineering; the hard part is recruiting a representative panel.

defensibility.rationale: A panel of hundreds of thousands of verified .edu students took years to build and is hard to copy quickly, though general pollsters could recruit students.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found copying it; the company partnered with Qualtrics and Inside Higher Ed according to its site and search results.

market_need_then: Klein told Dartmouth in 2017 that competitors had high caliber, which suggests an existing market, but no named competitors or spend figures were found; investors backed the seed in 2019.

branding.domain_note: Early product at pulsesurvey.com per Dartmouth in 2017; now collegepulse.com

rebrands.why: Dartmouth 2017 article calls the product Pulse and notes another site with that name; the rename date and reason were not found

brand_strength.rationale: Known in higher education media partnerships, but no sourced press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: College Pulse started as a Dartmouth student project in 2016, joined YC in Summer 2018 and raised a 1.5M seed led by Madrona in May 2019. Its panel grew to 800,000 or more students with partners like Qualtrics, and it is still operating as a small company. No acquisition or distress news was found.
notes: Seed date is May 1, 2019 per NHBR; other sources give April 23 or May 29, 2019. A Dartmouth project page says 1.35M and CB Insights says 1.62M over 3 rounds, unverified. Millworks Fund planned to invest 100K in 2017 per Dartmouth, a plan not confirmed as a closed round. No dated competitor names were found, so the list is empty. Panel size claims vary 450K to 850K across dates.
